image_summary: A photograph showing the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar, India, situated in the middle of a sacred pool (sarovar) with its distinctive gold-plated exterior and central dome reflecting in the water.
observed_clues: Large, central gilded structure with a prominent central dome
Surrounding water body reflecting the structure
White marble base level with intricate carvings
People visible walking on the causeway/pathway along the base
Orange flags typical of Sikh religious sites
Air conditioning units visible on the ground level of the structure
inferred_points: The site is a major pilgrimage center given the architectural grandeur and presence of devotees
The gold plating suggests high status and devotional significance in the Sikh faith
The presence of modern amenities like AC units indicates the site is actively maintained and used in a contemporary context

location_confidence.why: The structure is globally iconic and visually unmistakable.

signals: Authentic presence of human figures and minor functional details like AC units which are often present in the actual site photography

historical_context: The foundation was laid in the 16th century by Guru Arjan Dev. The current appearance, including the gold-plating of the upper levels, dates primarily from the 19th-century restoration commissioned by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
verified_facts: Harmandir Sahib is the holiest Gurdwara of Sikhism.
The temple is located in the city of Amritsar, Punjab, India.
The upper floors of the temple are covered with approximately 750kg of gold.
reasoning: The visual architectural features (central dome, gold-leaf structure, reflection in the sacred pool) are specific signatures of the Harmandir Sahib. The environmental context (Amritsar, Punjab) is consistent with the visual evidence.
additional_observations: Sky condition is clear blue with wispy clouds
The reflection in the water shows a realistic level of distortion and color depth
